Lessons.Title: School Community Garden (optional)
ExplanationParagraphs: This Grade3 U04 Lesson22 is OPTIONAL in the original 2021 edition; it has no new mathematical content standard and no Cool-down. Pupils use multiplication/division to plan garden beds with real contextual assumptions, not one numerical answer.

Warm-up original strawberry garden photo prompts discussion of plant arrangement, access, water, sunlight, expected yield and how to space plants. Source photos were checked visually on owner device but not copied into Edulytics.

Activity1 source strawberry patch contains7 rows of8 plants each→7×8=56 plants. Rows are4 feet apart and adjacent plants within rows2 feet apart. 12 strawberries per plant gives8×12=96 strawberries PER ROW. A first-party extension calculates56×12=672 across all rows, but the source only asks the harvest per row.

Dimensions caveat: if referring to distances from first to last PLANT CENTERS, seven row positions create six4-foot gaps=24 feet, and eight plant positions create seven2-foot gaps=14 feet. Garden footprint beyond the outermost plants requires margin assumptions not supplied in original; teacher reviews interpretations rather than asserts exact planted-bed dimensions.

Activity2 original six choices and planting rules: strawberries grow in patches,4-foot row spacing/2-foot plant spacing/12 fruits per plant; cantaloupes on vines,4-foot row/1-foot plant spacing/about8 each; zucchini on vines,5-foot rows/1-foot plants/about8; tomatoes on vines,4-foot rows/2-foot plants/about20; pinto beans in bushes,2-foot rows/1-foot plants/20–25 pods per plant and around5 beans per pod; potatoes in rows,2–3-foot row spacing/1-foot plants/5–10 potatoes per plant.

The ORIGINAL pupil task is to circle ANY TWO types and plan that EACH crop produces between50 and100 fruits or vegetables, showing total plants, arrangement, required spacing and harvest projection. Example INDEPENDENT design: strawberries6×12=72 and tomatoes4×20=80, subject to valid layout. There are many acceptable designs; source does not fix two plant types.

Because pinto beans make about100–125 beans per plant, choosing one bean plant may exceed100 and require explanation; potato yield5–10 is a range so ten potato plants might yield50–100. Teacher must check uncertainty, real-world planting assumptions and MLR7 Compare and Connect visual display.

This lesson is OPTIONAL and has no source Cool-down; don't fabricate one. Original student PDF and third-party photo rights were not individually certified. No Stage D, runtime tests, academic approval or complete original publisher parity claimed.

KeyConcepts.Title: Yield per row
KeyConcepts.Definition: Plants in a row multiplied by fruits per plant.

KeyConcepts.Title: Spacing
KeyConcepts.Definition: Distance between neighboring plant positions differs from bed edge dimensions.
KeyConcepts.Example: Seven row centers give24 feet across six4-foot gaps.

KeyConcepts.Title: Design constraints
KeyConcepts.Definition: Many plant choices can meet a harvest target with viable layout.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: State seven row centers are 7×4=28 feet apart.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Seven row positions have six intervals; 28-foot footprint would require an additional edge assumption.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Distinguish center-to-center24 feet from unknown full plot boundary.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treat garden plan as one fixed crop selection.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The source asks each pupil to choose two and justify both yields and layout.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Grade plan with a teacher rubric, not one answer key.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Presume pinto bean yields exactly20 beans per plant.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Source states20–25 pods with approximately5 beans each.

Seven rows×eight strawberry plants=56; eight plants×12=96 fruit per row.
Each of two freely selected crops must yield50–100 fruit/vegetables.
All six original crop requirements preserved; teacher evaluates layouts and assumptions.
